changes.headline: Crack correction: Friday's diesel close revises to $99.35; the $100 streak ended at nine days
changes.dek: Diesel crack $99.35 on the completed Oct 16 close (validated history refreshed Oct 18), revising the $104.35 printed Oct 17 from that morning's refresh; 37 total days above $100; all-time maximum $117.92 (Sep 16); 3-2-1 crack $55.15 (maximum $75.31, Aug 28).. The refreshed validated crack history puts Friday's completed diesel crack close at $99.35, not the $104.35 printed in Saturday's edition from that morning's data pull. On the validated series, Friday closed below $100 and the streak above $100 ended at nine days. The physical diesel facts are unchanged: a primary distillation unit at Russia's Ryazan refinery (about 340 kb/d) remains halted after Thursday's drone attack, no Russian diesel cargo has been reported loaded, Moscow's export ban runs through October, and US retail diesel averaged $6.33 per gallon on Friday. The crack remains historically extreme, but it is no longer streaking, and the IEA's accelerated release (remaining roughly 100 Mbbl, more than 20 Mbbl of it diesel, no published arrival timing) is still to arrive.
changes.balance_read: The tightest product signal softened at the margin on the week's biggest escalation day. Price and physics diverge by a crack-width: delivered barrels (IEA arrivals with dates, or a Russian cargo loading) resolve it; neither has printed.
changes.publishers: Validated crack history, refreshed Oct 18, 2026; Reuters, Oct 16, 2026 (Ryazan unit halt per industry sources; AAA retail diesel)

changes.headline: Canadian strip widens again Friday: December TMW -$27.40, back tenors down $1.05 to $1.20 on volume
changes.dek: ICE settles, Oct 16: TMW Dec26 -$27.40 (-$0.65, 1 lot, widest of the episode); Jan27 -$26.75, Feb27 -$25.20, Mar27 -$23.50, Apr27 -$21.95, May27 -$20.90, Jun27 -$20.15 (Apr-Jun 150 lots each); ARV Dec26 -$18.55 (-$0.65, 670 lots); ARV-TMW Dec unchanged at +$8.85; TMS Nov26 +$7.57 (+$0.02, zero volume); TMF Dec26 +$4.05.. Friday's ICE settlements file reached this run after Saturday's edition. December WCS made a new widest print of the episode at -$27.40, but on a single lot, against Thursday's -$26.75 on 805 lots, so the level is an indicative marker whose test is Monday's file. The traded widening sat in the back: January through June fell $1.05 to $1.20, with 150 lots in each of the April to June tenors, and WCS Houston December fell $0.65 on 670 lots while the ARV-TMW December spread held at +$8.85. SYN Nov26 settled at +$7.57, essentially unchanged, in the first session after the Syncrude coker turnaround window wrapped on Oct 16, holding above the pre-registered +$7.00 line ahead of the Oct 23 verdict.
changes.balance_read: The strip is pricing the winter egress and freight regime in the back tenors on real volume, not a prompt scramble at the front. December's thin print gets verified or revised by Monday's file and the November apportionment notice.
changes.publishers: ICE Report Center EOD, Oct 16, 2026; Enbridge apportionment notice, Sep 16, 2026 (standing reference)

changes.headline: Quiet Saturday: Friday's escalation settles stand; Riyadh resumption unconfirmed after NOTAM expiry
changes.dek: No fresh Hormuz attacks, Saudi developments, or flow updates verified for Oct 17; Riyadh King Khalid closure notice expired 21:00 GMT Oct 17 with no resumption confirmed as of early Oct 18; Hormuz shipments stand at 9.4 Mb/d (Kpler, week ended Wednesday).. Saturday produced no verified change to the war's barrel math. The last hard prints stand: Hormuz crude shipments at 9.4 Mb/d (about 70 percent of the pre-war average), at least nine ships attacked near the Strait since Sunday, MT ST 3 struck Friday with crew safe, a ballistic missile aimed at Yanbu intercepted with no infrastructure damage, and the IRGC mine claim still unverified. Riyadh's airport closure notice expired at 21:00 GMT Saturday; expiry is a schedule, not an operation, and no resumption had been confirmed by early Sunday, with several carriers suspended well beyond today. Friday's settles (Brent Dec26 $109.86, highest since May 19; WTI Nov26 $101.41, highest since Sep 17) carry an acknowledged weekend-risk premium into Monday's open.
changes.balance_read: A no-news weekend after an escalation Friday leaves the premium untested rather than confirmed. Monday's open is the verdict on the weekend component; the flow series (9.4 Mb/d and the next Kpler vintage) remains the gauge that matters.
changes.publishers: Reuters, Oct 16, 2026 (Friday settles; Kpler shipments); wire and official checks, Oct 18, 2026 (no fresh Oct 17 developments verified; Riyadh resumption unconfirmed)

flags.title: Hormuz shipments at 9.4 Mb/d; Friday's premium gets its Monday verdict
flags.detail: Kpler shipments averaged 9.4 Mb/d in the week ended Wednesday, about 70 percent of the pre-war average. At least nine ships have been attacked since Sunday and MT ST 3 was struck Friday; Yanbu was aimed at and intercepted. Saturday added no new damage, so part of Friday's settle is an untested weekend premium. The risk is clearance falling further or a strike hitting Saudi process, pipeline or export assets. Trigger: Hormuz shipments fall materially below 9.4 Mb/d, a strike hits Saudi process, pipeline or export assets, or Monday's open gives back the weekend component

flags.title: Crack slips below $100 on the validated close; regime break unconfirmed
flags.detail: The diesel crack closed at $99.35 on Friday (validated history, refreshed Oct 18), ending the streak above $100 at nine days; the $104.35 printed Saturday came from that morning's refresh and is superseded. Ryazan's primary distillation unit is halted and no Russian diesel cargo has loaded, but the IEA acceleration (remaining roughly 100 Mbbl, 20+ Mbbl of diesel) has no published arrival timing. The break confirms on arrivals and stock builds, neither of which has printed; a close back above $100 would read as a one-day break. Trigger: Further closes below $100 alongside published IEA arrival timing, a US distillate stock build, or a close back above $100

flags.title: SPR 40 Mbbl award still pending, twelve days after bids
flags.detail: No DOE announcement on the 40 Mbbl exchange as of early Sunday (DOE pages checked directly Oct 18). Posted contracts from the earlier rounds still show 133.56 Mbbl lent to 13 companies, Trafigura largest at about 34 Mbbl. The award, when it lands, prices 40 Mbbl of medium sour into the Gulf for November and December delivery. Trigger: DOE award announcement or a change to the posted SPR contracts

flags.title: Freight wall: Western heavies reprice together
flags.detail: The latest Baltic weekly (week ending Oct 9, pulled Oct 16) has TD9 (Caribbean to US Gulf Coast) at WS 1030, about $19.08/bbl estimated and up 51 percent on the week, with the USGC-to-China leg at $40.23/bbl against a Friday Brent-WTI settle spread of $8.45. High Caribbean-to-Gulf freight makes Venezuelan sellers captive to the Gulf, so Merey length is offered at deeper FOB discounts and pressures WCS Houston pricing whether it fills or not. The failed snap-back stands: Joliet restarted weeks ago and the differential did not rebound. Trigger: A fresh Merey FOB discount print, a TD9 move of 20 percent or more, or a WCS Houston response to a freight turn

forward_calendar.detail: Decides whether the binding-from-November base case is right; December TMW settled at -$27.40 on Oct 16 (ICE, 1 lot) ahead of it. The notice is a genuine information print: nobody knows the percentages until Enbridge publishes. October was 8 percent lights / 4 percent heavies at Kerrobert.

forward_calendar.what: Monday open after a no-news weekend; first full ICE file of the week
forward_calendar.detail: Friday's settles (Brent $109.86, WTI $101.41) carried an acknowledged weekend-risk premium and Saturday delivered no new damage, so Monday's open prices the weekend component. Monday's ICE file is also the first real test of December TMW's thin -$27.40 print (1 lot) and carries the second post-return SYN settle.
Front-month expiry mechanics sit inside the escalation tape; the Dec26 contract becomes the prompt read on flat price and on the Brent-WTI spread.

Scoring date for the pre-registered Syncrude return read: SYN Nov26 settled at +$7.57 on Oct 16, the first settle after the coker window wrapped. At or below +$6.50 within three business days of a clean return confirms the supply-return read; still above +$7.00 on Oct 23 scores the premium as priced-in or the return as slipped.

Bids went in Oct 6 (11:00 a.m. CT); a clean award prices 40 Mbbl of medium sour into the Gulf for Nov-Dec delivery. No award announced twelve days later (DOE pages checked directly Oct 18); DOE posted contracts still show 133.56 Mbbl lent to 13 companies in the earlier rounds, Trafigura largest at about 34 Mbbl.
Next scheduled OPEC+ meeting; quotas are not the constraint, actual supply is.
